note: raterB. Deleted 3 of the 7 mechanically extracted rows because they are not findings: n=1 'content discovery / attack-surface mapping' and n=2 'technology fingerprinting / auth model mapping' are recon inventories self-labelled 'No issue identified', and n=7 'missing function-level authorization (BFLA)' is a negative control self-labelled 'No issue identified' ('Function-level checks enforced') - the same treatment given to the other runs' 'classes tested and not proven' sections. The 4 surviving rows each assert a real issue but every one is self-labelled 'Requires further review', so under the rating instruction they are reported-row true positives with no truth-row credit. Result: recall 0.00 with precision 1.00 over 4 claims. That combination is a genuine property of a run that was cut off mid-engagement, not a rating accident; it is also the sharpest weakness of the rubric, which lets a run that proved nothing score a perfect precision off four hedged claims.
